title: Best Spreadsheet Software for Small Business (2026)
dek: For most small businesses, Google Sheets is the best value for collaboration and Excel wins for analysis. Zoho, LibreOffice, WPS, OnlyOffice, Numbers, Airtable and Coda round out the best free and paid alternatives. Here is how to choose.

seo.metaTitle: Best Spreadsheet Software for Small Business
seo.metaDescription: Best spreadsheet software plus free Excel and Google Sheets alternatives, compared on price, collaboration and ease of use — a pick for each need.

richText: The best spreadsheet software for a small business is the one your team will actually use together, at a price that fits. For most, that is Google Sheets for its unbeatable collaboration; for finance-heavy work, Excel is worth the extra cost. But there is a strong field of free and paid alternatives — from LibreOffice and Zoho to Airtable and Coda. This guide compares the main options and the best free Excel and Google Sheets alternatives, and tells you who each one suits.

body.richText: Pricing tiers change often. Treat the price column as a guide and confirm the current plan on each vendor's own pricing page before you buy.

body.text: Best overall for most small businesses: Google Sheets

body.richText: Google Sheets, on its own or as part of Workspace, gives a small team real-time collaboration, automatic saving, easy sharing, and version history. There is almost nothing to manage and nothing to install, and it is free for individuals. For the majority of small businesses, it is the most productive, lowest-friction choice.

body.text: Best for finance and analysis: Microsoft 365 (Excel)

body.text: When you have outgrown a plain grid: Airtable and Coda

richText: If your spreadsheet has really become a mini-database — tasks, projects, inventory — Airtable and Coda add structure a flat grid cannot: linked records, multiple views (kanban, calendar), and automations. items.question: What is the cheapest spreadsheet software for a small business?
items.answerRichText: LibreOffice Calc is completely free, and Google Sheets is free for individuals (a small monthly cost per user under Workspace unlocks business features). Zoho Sheet and WPS also have strong free tiers.

items.question: What is the best free alternative to Excel?
items.answerRichText: For collaboration, Google Sheets. For an offline desktop app with no account, LibreOffice Calc. Zoho Sheet, WPS, and OnlyOffice are also free and open .xlsx files, so your pick depends on whether you work online or offline.

items.question: What is the best free alternative to Google Sheets?
items.answerRichText: Zoho Sheet is the closest free, browser-based match, with real-time collaboration. For offline work, LibreOffice Calc or Apple Numbers are the top free choices.

items.question: Can free spreadsheet software open Excel (.xlsx) files?
items.answerRichText: Yes. Google Sheets, LibreOffice Calc, Zoho Sheet, WPS, OnlyOffice, and Apple Numbers all open and save .xlsx files. Very complex macros or advanced formatting may not carry over perfectly, so test important files.
